label: Jamnapari

names.text: Alternative names from the Wikipedia article. Etawah is listed there as a name used in Indonesia, not a name for the breed, so it is left out.

about.text: The Jamnapari is a large Indian milk goat from the Etawah District of Uttar Pradesh. It is one of the ancestors of the Anglo-Nubian. Its milk is used for dairy, and its meat is also used.

sources.text: Origin, ancestry of the Anglo-Nubian, and milk and meat uses from the Wikipedia article (fetched with WebFetch).

origin.place: The Braj region of Uttar Pradesh, specifically the Etawah District and the Chakarnagar tehsil. Distribution is also listed in Madhya Pradesh, with Indonesia and Bangladesh.

sources.text: Origin region, place and distribution from the Wikipedia article (fetched with WebFetch). No founding history is given, so no formed dates are entered.
The 1972 Indian census estimate of goats of this breed, as the article gives it. The article also says fewer than 5,000 were thought to be purebred.
The article lists the uses as milk and meat, and does not mention draught use.
DAD-IS (2021) status as the Wikipedia article reports it. The article also gives FAO (2007) as not at risk.

facts.v: Slightly less than two kilograms a day on average

sources.text: The average daily lactation yield as the article states it, with no total lactation figure.

facts.v: One of the ancestors of the Anglo-Nubian goat

sources.text: Stated in the article's history section.

facts.v: Conception rates of nearly 90 percent, with triplets and quadruplets common

gaps: No total lactation yield, lactation length, or milk composition figures were found on the Wikipedia article. No founding history was given. No FAO DAD-IS world population beyond the 1972 census estimate was found, and that figure is an estimate of goats of the breed, not a current count.
